message.content: Both accuracy claims (c1: catastrophic cancellation, c2: roundoff accumulation) remain inconclusive, and the two probes designed to decide them (t12, t13) failed due to the probes' own input-generation bugs rather than any kernel behavior. Since these are the material in-scope risks and are still testable, I'll request another debate round to get corrected probe coverage rather than settle prematurely.

function.arguments: {"focus_claims": ["c1", "c2"], "reason": "Claims c1 (catastrophic cancellation in FP32 numerators) and c2 (accumulated FP32 roundoff) are still inconclusive: the extreme-cancellation probe t8 only exercised symmetric products that cancel exactly, and the two sharper follow-up probes (t12, t13) aborted on their own input-generation bugs (infinite FP16 values and an FP32-typed tensor), not on any kernel behavior. The contract covers every finite FP16 combination with a tight per-component tolerance, so asymmetric-cancellation and skewed-denominator cases are decisive in-scope inputs that have not yet been tested. Need corrected probes: for c1, generate finite-FP16 near-cancellation rows with asymmetric products (e.g. d = -a*c/b clipped to the FP16 grid, or perturbed by one FP16 ulp); for c2, fix the dtype bug (ensure .to(torch.float16) after skewing) and rerun the no-cancellation/skewed-denominator worst-case search."}
